$comment: What the UPSTREAM provider charges Kaana, per deployment. Optional: with no rate card file, provider cost is not measured, and every measurement says so rather than reporting zero.

This is not a customer price and never becomes one. Oxy owns every customer-facing amount today (Oxy ADR 0006; Kaana ADR 0010 proposes moving it); Kaana measures units, reports them, and separately records what its providers will invoice it. Nothing here reaches a stream event, a usage report or an error body — see internal/providercost.

amountPerUnit is an integer in 1e-12 of the currency's major unit, the same scale as the published contract's money type so an operator reconciling an invoice against the ledger is comparing like with like. A provider quoting $2.50 per million input tokens is 2500000 here.

Every unit a deployment can report should be priced. A unit that is measured and not priced is named in the measurement rather than silently treated as free, so a reconciliation cannot look complete while being short.

A cache WRITE has its own unit, cache_write_input_tokens (the default 5-minute write). A card that does not list it names the unit unpriced instead of costing it at nothing, so list it, from the provider's own documented rate (Anthropic: 1.25x the base input rate), when a deployment writes to a prompt cache. See docs/cost.md, Cache-write tokens.
The numbers below are invented placeholders. No provider's real rates are published in this repository.

Each file is one immutable rate-card version. rateCardVersionId names it, source says where the prices came from (provider_api, provider_documentation or operator), and the version is registered append-only in PostgreSQL at startup: a changed price must ship under a new rateCardVersionId, and reusing an id with different prices stops the process.
